rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Parent-chain + locant(s) + sub-prefix + suffix = IUPAC name

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ treat "Purification" as one blob → ✅ split into: purification, qualitative, quantitative analysis of organic compounds.  ·  ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: IUPAC: identify parent chain (longest), number from end nearer the functional group / first substituent; suffix by priority (−ol, −al, −one, −oic acid…).  ·  Carbocation/carbanion stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl; resonance stabilises; inductive effect transmits through sigma bonds.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Purification method picker — sublimation (camphor, benzoic acid), crystallisation (impure sugar), distillation (liquid with b.p. difference), fractional distillation (close b.p.), steam distillation (oils immiscible with water), differential extraction (solubility difference).  ·  Trick 2: Lassaigne's test: fuse with Na → NaCN (N), Na2S (S), NaX (halogen); N + S together → NaSCN — the three conversions are the core answer.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Trick 3: Qualitative N test: Prussian blue Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3; S: violet with sodium nitroprusside or black with lead acetate; halogens: AgNO3 colours (white/cream/pale yellow).  ·  Trick 4: Quantitative C and H: Liebig combustion — %C = (12/44)(mass CO2/mass sample)×100, %H = (2/18)(mass H2O/mass)×100 — two ratios, two answers.  ·  define + example each sub-idea: purification, qualitative, quantitative analysis of organic compounds.
